clauses.text: Any being in the game, including a player’s character, is a creature.

relations.evidence: Every creature, including every player character, has a tag in the rules that identifies the type of creature it is.

summary: GLOSS.creature is a single definition: every being in the game, player characters included, is a creature. It has one testable clause: a PC counts as a creature for any rule that targets or refers to creatures. It points to GLOSS.creature-type, which gives every creature (PCs included) exactly one type tag (R-38, R-39). I found no ambiguities, conflicts, gaps or 2014 traps worth recording. "Being" isn't defined further, but the creature types (Construct, Undead, Ooze, Plant) already settle the borderline cases.
